title: Worlds of Magic
text: First off, the game is meant to be a spiritual successor to Master of Magic.  I haven't played that game since it came out so my memory is not great.  I do see some of the influences though.  I'll let someone else make more comparisons there. What do I like about the game? 1.  Setting:  I am a sucker for fantasy games and this is pure fantasy all the way through.  The various planes on which you can battle are well represented. 2.  Graphics:  Overall, I like the graphics.  The animations are sometimes a bit stilted but overall I like it.  I particularly like seeing each city on the city screen evolve as I add more buildings. 3.  Combat:  It's turn-based and d20 so you kind of feel like you're playing out an RPG battle at times.  I do feel cheated on occasion by the dice rolls but anyone who played D&D will understand that feeling. 4.  Spells:  There are a ton of these, as there should be.  They run the usual RPG gamut from buffs to DOT's to direct damage spells and are nicely presented. Overall, you get a nice variety of races that play differently, a ton of fantasy type enemies to battle against, and all the 4X you can soak up.  Are there bugs?  Sure.  Is it perfect?  No.  But I strongly believe in the development team based on their support so far.  If you're looking for turn based strategy, fantasy, or a 4X game, you should definitely give this a try.

title: Worlds of Magic
text: World of Magic, I want to like this game, I loved MOM (Masters of Magic), but alas this game falls far short of the original game.  The tutorials will get you going quickly if you are not familiar with the game.  But for those of us that are old hands at 4x games it does not really re-invent the wheel.  It is what you would expect if someone was to re-make MOM, though I wish the developers spent a little more effort giving it some innovation rather than going for a port/clone. Graphics are what you would expect from a 4x game, nothing special but adequate, getting into the game is easy enough, play the tutorial, pick your faction, modify the world as you can and away you go.  The issue is you don’t go fast, development is slower than molasses.  In fact most of the games I played I was wiped out by the Neutral war bands before I could get into the game.  Another issue was even at the lower levels the various structures had monsters so high I could not even think about attacking.  Of course that is when I could interact with them.  There seems to have been a bug in one game that was actually go well, only to find structures empty and could not interact with them. If you are looking to add 4x game to your library I would skip this one. I wish the team would pay a bit attention to the game, it feels like it needs a major balancing in all aspects of the game.  Here is a list of what I feel needs to be addressed. 1.	Structure bugs with buildings you can interact with.  You can’t always interact with them as typically this is a major source of goodies this needs to be fixed. 2.	Mobs should scale to the level of game you are playing, or at least giving the player a bonus in order to survive the early game. 3.	Neutral mobs should be just that Neutral, why are they attacking early in the game, when my settlements are barely off the ground. 4.	Tweak the economics especially at the adept and Mageling levels trying to build cities and expand is part of the game, but barely scraping by with gold should not be an issue.  While you are trying to balance your budget, the Neutral mobs seem to have unlimited funds to build the stronger units earlier than you can. This game needs more work, there is a gem in there, but only 5/10 is the rating I give it.

text: This is a review of the Early Access Game.   I personally have been enjoying the game and it does remind me a lot of MOM. I recommend the game with reservations:    Know that this game is not done, you may have issues/bugs, and saves may be corrupted with new updates.  I have been able to play for the last few hours without any crashes or issues (others have reported some issue, likely related to their specific systems.     If you know what you are getting into, it can be great fun. If you have played and enjoy MOM in the past, you should like this game as well (it plays very similarly).   If you haven't, it plays much like many of the 4x fantasy games such as AOW, HOMM but more in a "you against all others" kind of way.  There are no real scenarios;  just start up in a random world and explore, expand and conquer.    Diplomacy doesn't do much for me yet. I have been part of a dozen or so EA (early access) games and these developers have been one of the best at communication and updates, as well as responding well to user input.     They give me confidence that they will follow through and make this a great finished product.   I will keep this updated as time goes on.  Thumbs up for now (but please be aware, the product is not finished)

title: Worlds of Magic
text: Planar Conquest is the remake of Worlds of Magic, which is the spiritual sequel to Master of Magic. Worlds of Magic was kickstarted, but then picked up by a distributor, which forced the developers to release the game before it was finished. They worked hard to fix all of the problems, but in the end, working from the ground up was the faster route. The result if very good. It is the closest game to Master of Magic I've played in years. It doesn't have the same level of polish as a bigger studio would give it, but it has the heart or what made Master of Magic the ultimate "just one more turn" game.

title: Worlds of Magic
text: The short version is that this game was released far, far too early and it's riddled with gamestopping bugs. It's also devoid of personality, has incredibly horrible balance, a UI that should have been trashed and a host of other issues. Read on for more information but avoid this turd at all costs. --- Wastelands, I like you guys. I was rooting for you guys. But I've given up and uninstalled. Perhaps I'll check it out in 6 months but at this juncture WoM is unplayable. I hate to use a term like that but I there's nothing else that adequately describes it. Note that I test all bugs twice before reporting them. That's key - I don't report bugs that I can't duplicate. So the errors below could be duplicated by loading the save file and doing the same actions again. On my first attempt to play post-release combat didn't work. So I put it down for a few days. My second attempt (this Monday) ended when I took a city and the game froze. Today I go to load up that save file to name it before sending it in and find that it's been corrupted post the 1.0.3 patch. I'm pretty disappointed since I could at least play the game prior to launch. Now it's just...unplayable. What else could you call it? I love MoM and wanted this to work enough to buy it while in EA. But at this stage there's no use even trying to play it because it simply doesn't work for me. How can I not be at least a little frustrated with you when many people, including me, were trying to politely caution you against releasing too early? From my standpoint - yours may be different - this looks like it was released far too early. Now the devs have done some patching in the last month but many, many core issues remain. Not only are there bugs but throw in a horrid UI, a real lack of any strategy beyond spam cities (kind of a killer in a "strategy" game), subpar animations, really uninteresting tactical combat...the whole package is a big pile of poo. Now they're working on this to bring it to mobile devices, so don't expect it to get any better.

But what is currently done is nothing less than spectacular.  As someone who wasted weeks and months of my life playing MoM back in the 9s, I can see how amazing this game will be. title: Wuppo
text: Wuppo: ~~~~~~ Who would have believed that eating ice cream could earn you an eviction notice? Well, to be fair with Carlo, the Wum at the Wum House service desk, it’s not fun at all cleaning ice cream off the beautiful rugs at the entrance and on the fourth level. Especially now, when all the cleaners have run away to Popocity. It’s only part of the reason; the real reason is that Carlo dislikes cleaning (I’m with you, Carlo), but throwing a Wum out of the Wum House for this, it’s a tad extreme. Hey Wuppo! Did you hear what I say? You have to find a new place to live. Well, start cracking! Wuppo is a platformer/adventure game with good puzzles where you control a cute, round character who has four legs and can make great double jumps. He is part of the Wum race, who are the most intelligent of four main species in the world, but lack of abilities.  The other three races are the Blussers, Splenkhakkers and the nasty Fnakkers. You’ll meet a bird, “Denksnavel,” fairly quickly in the game. This bird will give you hints every time you select him. The Allesweters is another character who you will be talking a fair bit with and can be found in different locations. He has a projector and can play the filmstrips collectable items you’ll find within the world. The world is extremely well-designed with great locations to discover, and it’s not hard to navigate. Within the main places, you’ll have to help other Wums or species to move forward in the game. Some will be challenging puzzles and others will lead to a fight with big, scary monsters! Please don’t scare the kawum out of me! When you successfully help these characters and make them happy, you’ll be rewarded with extra health points and items which in turn will help you to resolve the next puzzle or challenges in the world. There is a fair bit of reading in this game and you really need to take your time to go through it or you will miss important information. Bear in mind that you can come back to individuals and re-asked questions. The dialogue is really fun and you can select different answers when you interact with each creature. In some of the destinations, you’ll find stores where you can buy or sell items using the smurt currency. You can obtain additional smurts either by helping other individuals, or when you kill enemies. For me the game shines in the puzzles. However, you’ll be fighting interesting bosses and some are not that easy to eliminate. Oh, by the way, you’ll be armed with a GumGumGun which shoots coloured gums. There is a place where you can upgrade your weapons at a specific store in Popocity. Splendid artwork and the soundtrack is very cute. For the controls, whether you use the mouse and keyboard or the gamepad, they work fine and it is very easy to allocate binding keys to your inventory. Positives: ~~~~~~~ -	Splendid artwork -	Well-designed world -	Great puzzles -	Fun fighting bosses -	Fun dialogues -	Achievements and trading cards Negatives: ~~~~~~~~ -	 I think the fighting bosses could be a notch harder This game is a gem - thoroughly entertaining and fun to play! 8/10 Key provided by developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

title: Wuppo
text: Wuppo is a mixed bag, the game has amazing characters, a great world and a nice general story but it lacks in gameplay, pacing and interface. At first i absolutely loved this game, because the introduction of the game is really well done, the interaction between the main character and the hotelier is hilarious. My love for the game quickly faded when it turned out that the gameplay is mostly superficial platforming and point & click style puzzles with a couple of nice bossfights thrown in there. Gameplay: The first puzzle was already confusing, there are 4 pictures of different races below a switch puzzle, however you had to throw random items on these. I really don't know how they thought a cooking pot resembles a race that looks like a potato. Sure you have a bird that can sometimes be helpful he basically tells you what to do for the first puzzle but as often he can obfuscate the solution even further. In a later puzzle where you need to summon a dude the bird says the dude can't be summoned right now, so i thought well maybe i have do something else first, turns out he could be summoned you just need to turn off the lights again. That is how i generally felt about the game, i had no idea where to go or what to do most of the time, so i just wandered around aimlessly until i found something to do, reminding me more and more of point and click games – a genre i hate. Other gameplay issues are that you can run out of money to buy an item that is necessary to beat  the game. In Popocity you need to buy an item and there are some jobs you can do to get money, however eventually these jobs become unavailable and then you have no way to get enough money other than going back to old areas and gather some money there which is boring and slow and i was almost ready to abandon the game right there. Pacing: While the characters and the story are amazing, the pacing isn‘t. Throughout the game you can find filmstrips and because money is always tight you have to pretty much watch all of them because you get money as a reward for watching them, they are usually long and boring reading sections, wouldn‘t be so bad if it was voiced or funny cutscenes but it is just huge textboxes with a little picture in the background. Right before you are ready to fight the final boss they slap you in the face with a 10 minute read about how the Wuppo world functions. User-interface: I wouldn‘t recommend playing this game with a controller, i couldn‘t find a good keybinding steup to make the platforming and using items work in a good way. It is better with mouse and keyboard because you can assign hotkeys to items but it still feels off. Probably because the mouse-wheel scrolls through every single item you have ever collected instead of just the ones you have hotkeyed? Or maybe i dislike it because you can‘t aim properly in this game and you can‘t hit an enemy that is directly in front of you? Or maybe i dislike that they designed some menu-items for a controller and others for mouse and keyboard? Maybe a little bit of all of these, it just doesn't feel right. To summarize my experience in one sentence: In Wuppo you go through a bunch of frustrating puzzles for two hours to have a 2 minute fun interaction with an NPC and a cool 5 minute boss fight.

title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
text: Despite all of the lavish praise this game received, I can't recommend it. I played the original XCOM on a 486dx33 (yes a 33mhz processor) and loved it.  I will go right to the heart of my grudge against XCOM: Enemy Unknown.  Enemies drop into your battles at random locations, including behind your squad's positions.  This wrecks use of cover.  It wrecks tactical positioning.  It wrecks immersion.  It might be okay if this were a rare thing that happened with certain enemies, but it is a central part of the system.  In my mind, nothing they do right could make up for such a terribly lazy implementation that substitutes randomness for a smart ai and well designed maps. For example, you are cautiously advancing your squad down a linear hallway deeper into the enemy base.  You are careful to keep them always behind cover for the direction you are advancing.  Maybe you also try to ensure that each squad member is appropriately positioned to use their weapon to full advantage.  You open a door, ready for your doorkicker assault members to burst in and scan for targets.  Suddenly a giant and very strong UFO shaped enemy drops immediately behind you in the hallway that you just cleared!  It takes its turn immediately and blasts your weakly armored sniper that you had left towards the rear.  They are now dead. Where did this UFO thing come from?  How can it just fall out of the sky?  What is the point of moving as a team if enemies simply drop in anywhere?  How can you use cover if enemies drop immediately behind your cover with no rhyme or reason?  This is terrible game design!  There would be nothing at all wrong with randomly spawning enemies at the start of the battle, but randomly dropping them into the fight is bad design. Other things missing that the original XCOM (1994) had: fully destructible terrain, fires, a beautiful and working light system (light grenades, fires cast light, etc) that made night missions terrifying, an alien rocket launcher with projectiles that could fly waypoints, freely flying armor, multiple troop carriers to research and build, the ability to set up multiple bases strategically around the globe, potentially catastrophic invasions of your bases, interceptor flight tracking, squad inventory management, etc etc etc.  Also, your characters weren't locked into any specific class nor did they have a radically dumbed-down and simplistic choose-one-of-two skill system. I remember all of these things even though I haven't played the game in many years because it was the little things like that combined with the awesome tactical combat that made XCOM so memorable and made for the sort of nostalgia that a cheap rip-off like this exploits to sell copies.  Few will remember this game in a few years, but the memory of the original X-COM remains. For a game that lacks so much of whats it's predecessors had, and messes up the core tactical combat, it is amazing to me that it has received such praise.

title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
text: I've never played the XCOM franchise before this game so I cannot compare this one to it's predecesors and neither can I judge the franchise as a whole, but I WILL tell you that this is an amazingly fun strategy game. As you can see from the store page; you are the leader of a worldwide anti-alien organisation and it's up to YOU to keep your troops alive and save the planet from their invasion. IN SHORT: GOOD + The gameplay starts of quite simple but get's more complex and incredibly hard later on, especially on higher difficulties! Great game to just step into without any prior information. No manual needed. + First playthrough took me over 40 hours to beat. + Simple but engaging story. Aliens invade earth and you're going to stop them. Characters are a bit stereotypical, but the voice acting and music make it all very endearing and fun. + Atmosphere is incredible for a top-down turn based game. You really feel the pressure of surviving and trying to complete your objective with little to no casualties. Every decision feels heavy and important; they really nailed that feeling here. + Mission variation. There is not a whole lot of it, but the many different maps, scenario's and objectives make it a fun experience for most of the playthrough. Might get a bit repetitive later on if you're trying to max out everything in your base though, expect to do some grinding for that. + Overal Quality. It's a very polished game with good graphics and great interface. The tutorial is short but sufficient and the rest speaks for itself. + Creating and customizing your own team is SUPER FUN. There arent a billion options to choose from but it's fleshed out enough to make you spend some time trying to recreate you best friends as supersoldiers! + The Enemy Within DLC is actually worth buying. It's not as great of an expension as say the Elder Scrolls games. But still a bunch of extra content worthy to give the game another playthrough or two. + The aliens are cool and unique. They all have their own strengths and weaknesses and figuring out how to deal with them best while doing scientific research about their bioligy feels as if you're really fighting an unknown enemy that you're slowly starting to understand better. + Quite long. Quite hard. Expect to spend a lot of time on this one. NOT SO GOOD - Since this is a turn-based strategy game where your chance to hit is a roll of the dice, expect to get frustrated sometimes when your sniper with 95% accuracy misses 2 shots in a row. Can feel unfair, especially on higher difficulties. - After all aliens and weapons are introduced the game goes on for quite a while. More unlocks or enemies would make it feel less bland and repetitive near the end. - Though there's quite a lot of dialogue in the game, expect your collegues to repeat themselves a bit too much through the course of the game. - Though there is some variation in the missions, there are basically only 3 kinds: Exterminate all forces, save civilians or disarm the bomb. It's enough variation for the beginning of the game but can get really bland if you're playing too long in one sitting. I suggest taking breaks from this game so it feels more stimulating. - Story begins and ends rather abrubtly with little to no explenation to motives or origin of the aliens. - Even though I said earlier that the Enemy Within DLC is fun, it's also kinda bland without it. All the most awesome stuff like Mechs and and Geneticly-Enhanced soldiers are within the DLC so buying this game without it seems like a waste and you'll never want to replay the vanilla game again without it. - Even though Multiplayer let's you take control of aliens as well, there's not much reason to stick around after you've finished the single player campaign. I know some people LOVE the multiplayer though, so this is just my personal opinion. And that's it for XCOM, I hope this review helped you out! If you have any questions be sure to leave a comment!

If this game had 10x the weapon selections and tech paths to allow more customization, it would be much more interesting. Enemy Within fixes many problems with this game, and improves on it.

title: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
text: Xcom is widely known to be an exceptional game. I would agree absolutely with that general concensus that this is a really decent tactical strategy game.  I can almost see what this is based on and where it has come from.  This version too exhibits some really nice additions which allows me to say with absolute confidence that technology made this game better.  In saying that there are issues with this game's quality and its design, and irronically Firaxis are getting no better at making games that are flawless... and that is worth saying as these are integral parts of the game I can  see that don't work/don't give enough feedback/ or just are buggy as hell, and it doesn't feel like it will get fixed at all. The beauty of Xcom Enemy Unknown is that is has so many sides to it.  It is in everyway, like Divinity : Dragon Commander, where you manage your ship, build stuff, get reserach, monitor stuff, build more stuff  in between tactical battle mode.  This design is brilliant can offer so much depth I think, and Dragon Commander went a step further in many cases.  I will add that Xcom's implementation of that is no different and allows you to do all sorts, though from what I can see, if you dont get this stuff by a certain time in the game, the game seems to suffocate your operation... not sure about that exactly,  but it felt like I 'nearly' did and it cost me at some point throughout the game.  Whats more, as Dragon Commander's Political exploits are generally not required in your 10th game, alot of the stuff on here is not time draining and does NOT keep you from getting into what XCom is all about.  Combat. Combat is decent and has reasonable depth and certainly does not get overloaded with stuff.  Its seamless, nice to do and leaves you little to worry about in your decisions.  improvements of weapons are worth it, improvement of the skills of each soldier is worth it , and when you get to a stage in the game where some of you soldiers get 'extra skillls'?  It's definately worth it.  However when its late game and your waiting to 'get paid', battle mode does feel like a chore sometimes, it restricts progress. Each of the classes to some extent feel like they are worth using, though the best ones at the start feel weak at the end, and the weak classes at the start feel OP at the end. What adds to this is the camera system, when an order is made, the camera follows your soldier, or some cinematic view is taken.  This is not something I would comment as being essential, but as it doesn't break anything and it looks good, gives  the game a nicer feel, it defeintely is good overall and gives the game a nice sheen. Now what I don't like about Xcom: Firaxis, have had a few gmes I have played with certain bugs and broken functionality, Xcom is no different.  As amazing as Xcom looks, and runs, Firaxis clearly didn't get the engine right.. There is a serious issue with the selection of parts of the map that you are not looking at ... for example, I can be looking at the interior of a ship and then click inside to move, and the system will think I the roof tile (above)or lower floor(below), potentially screwing up tactics(yes which is the difference between something going horribly wrong!)and the game (Diablo Hardcore characters and poor connection come to mind, and yes you can play hardcore on this - no saves!). I guess there is a cure, if you are pretentous enough to challenge that assertion, as you will need to look carefully where the point is and where the path fidning trail is.  This generally means, you have to zoom out, rotate the view blah blah... all in all its a bit of BS.. waste of time and does takes from the game. This should not happen if you are not zoomed to another 'layer' in my oppinion, and I think that is just logical.  I think if Firaxis thought about this issue, then they could have included an undo move button function, but they didn't... There are other issues with seeing the range of your units and what they can attack as it is not clear at all what you can attack and what you can until you move that unit... Also as far as i can see, you cannot pick your squad, i.e. if I want to train up a bunch of noob soldiers instead of using vets , then I can't, it's simple... Well, I could of course make sure (the vets) all take mortal wounds last match so they are off in the infirmary nursing wounds, but nothing more from looks of it.  Then in addition to that, when they are removed from the squad without wounds, the equipment stays on the soldier... Sometimes those soldiers dont show up in the team for the next mission, so you have 1 soldier with no gear (perhaps returning from the infirmary)and another one in the barracks that you have to track down and strip of their gear, and you CAN'T switch them... makes for boring cheese and bad design if you ask me... and yes, some equiptment mid game is damn expensive, so it is important that this works! Science is a let down, like supcom2, once you researched everything, you have wasted money on labs and scientists are in-effect worthless, it is very dis-empowering, and as much as your squad is powerful enough and the rest is justifiably left up to you to be a good strategist, it still makes for something of an empty concept... Civ and Alpha Centurai had post science qualifications.. I think they could have added those in to make an intersting endgame of sorts, making science a worth while endeavour. The story was alright I guess and the game flows much like Unreal 3, so its not complicated, but its good, and the art design definately complements that with the idea of who the alien race really is and where your going. There are some bad parts to this game , and as many people will rave blindly with the 'horde', I feel its nesscessary to point out Xcom is NOT perfect.  However, as a game, I spent 50+ hours  on this and I could play it again.  It was generally fun to play, so I would say most of the hype is infact justified. I will add, that I would definately consider gettin Xcom 2 at near full price as I liked this one so much.
